intervals.label: concept proposed (superfluid helium, calorimetric readout) and R&D
intervals.note: Start is the arXiv submission of the concept paper (15 Oct 2018); the proposal to host HeRALD at LSM as part of TESSERACT dates from 2022.
intervals.quote: We name this concept “HeRALD”, helium roton apparatus for light dark matter.

intervals.label: planned installation of the TESSERACT setups (including HeRALD) at LSM
intervals.note: A schedule; the setups are the two TESSERACT cryostats hosting SPICE, HeRALD and Ge/Si modules.
intervals.quote: The two setups will be in LSM between 2027 and 2028

placements.note: Proposed placement: the HeRALD module of the TESSERACT payload at LSM; the prototype work was done at UC Berkeley and UMass Amherst (not Atlas sites).
placements.quote: Combined with the US-based SPICE and HeRALD technologies, the TESSERACT at LSM experiment will then allow to probe DM candidates over 12 orders of magnitude in mass

target_medium.quote: HeRALD will use sensors with silicon or sapphire substrates to image radiative and quasiparticle emission from a target of superfluid helium-4 .

summary.plain: A cell of superfluid helium viewed from above by superconducting sensors that register the flash of light and the helium atoms knocked out of the liquid surface by a dark matter collision.
summary.technical: Superfluid 4He cell (HeRALD v0.1: 2.75 cm high, 6 cm diameter, ~10 g He) facing a photon/4He TES calorimeter wafer; a Cs-coated film stopper blocks superfluid film flow so the sensor stays dry.

technology.quote: The experiment consists of a superfluid helium target where DM particles would undergo nuclear recoil interactions.
technology.value: Superfluid helium-4 target read out by TES calorimeters (scintillation and quantum-evaporation channels)
